newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian energy body expects cut in pipeline tariff.
newsitem.headline: Russian energy body expects cut in pipeline tariff.

text.p: Russia's Federal Energy Commission (FEC) expects oil and oil product pipeline tariffs to be cut by 20 percent in May, Pavel Serikov, head of the FEC's price regulation section said on Thursday.

"We expect a reduction in May of around 20 percent (in oil and product transport tariffs)," he said. Serikov said he did not expect the tarriff cut to influence the amount of oil and products Russian oil companies exported.
"I don't think that the cut would affect the amount of exports," he said. "Most of the main pipeline routes for exports from Russia are already full."
He said that the Druzhba pipeline system which crosses Ukraine was not full to capacity, but that high Ukrainian transport tariffs would prevent any significant increase in exports via this route.
A source at the FEC said that the average cost of transporting one tonne of crude oil one kilometre on Russian soil was around 20 roubles.
The FEC was set up to introduce more market economy elements into energy exports and tariffs.
State-owned monopoly Transneft controls Russia's sprawling pipeline system, which includes around 50,000 km (31,000 miles) of crude oil routes and 20,500 km (12,700 miles) of oil product routes.
Serikov said that the tariff cut would help Russian oil companies, who have complained that pipeline tariffs are too high in Russia.
In total Russian exports 105 million tonnes of crude oil (2.1 million bpd) outside the Commonwealth of Independent States in 1996, up nine percent from 96 million tonnes (1.9 million bpd) in 1995.
Non-CIS oil product exports also rose to 55 million tonnes (1.1 million bpd) in 1996 from 44 million tonnes (880,000 bpd) in 1995.
